title: Helen Frankenthaler's birth chart
metaDescription: Helen Frankenthaler's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 20.4° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.1° separates Venus and Jupiter from an exact square; at that range taste and expansion read as one mechanism. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 20.4° Sagittarius — deep enough in the third decan (20°–30°) that the Sun, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 17.2° Sagittarius, Venus was at 0.8° Aquarius, Mars was at 2.9° Cancer. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that begins as conversation; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Venus at right angles from Jupiter, 0.1° off exact. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mars square Uranus at 0.5°, and Jupiter trine Neptune at 0.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. Mercury in Sagittarius at 17.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Cancer at 2.9° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements fire 4, water 2, earth 2, air 1; modalities mutable 4, cardinal 3, fixed 2. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Mars, Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde. Uranus changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.8° between one midnight and the next. Which of the two it was depends entirely on the hour, and the hour is not recorded. Rather than pick the likelier half, the reading leaves the Moon open.
